clue.text: Disparage exercise to discover the secret

parts.note: to disparage is to decry, run down
PT is physical training, i.e. exercise

explanation.surface: Belittling a workout routine somehow reveals a hidden truth.
explanation.definitionFit: To decode a cipher is to uncover its hidden message, its secret.

clue.text: Back last runner, which failed to start

parts.note: the last part of anything is its end

indicators.note: the runner's word loses its opening letter, as a horse that fails to start

parts.note: a horse is a runner in a race

explanation.surface: A punter backs the final horse, which then never leaves the stalls.
explanation.definitionFit: To back a candidate or cheque is to support or sign it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Cut the cake and have a dance

indicators.note: the cake's name is cut short, losing its last two letters

parts.note: a rum baba is a small yeast cake soaked in rum syrup

explanation.surface: Someone slices the party cake, then takes to the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' trims BA from the end of RUMBABA.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cuban ballroom dance in quadruple time, so an example of a dance.

clue.text: Purest article devised by a scientist

indicators.note: the letters are devised into a new arrangement, signalling an anagram

parts.note: A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A scientist comes up with the purest piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devised' rearranges PURESTA.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Pasteur was the French chemist and microbiologist behind pasteurisation, an example of a scientist.

indicators.note: one piece is added to the other, placed after it

parts.note: garb is clothing, dress
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Someone protests that it takes ages to get dressed, calling it nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' signals that one piece is attached after the other; the surface's 'Time to dress' reads as a single phrase but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Garbage is household waste, a straight synonym of rubbish, and also means nonsense.

clue.text: Sky pilot displaying a bit of religious mania

indicators.note: displaying is read as putting on show in a new arrangement, signalling an anagram
only a small bit, the opening letter, of religious is taken

explanation.surface: A chaplain, known as a sky pilot, shows a touch of zealotry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit of' gives R from religious; 'displaying' rearranges R with MANIA. 'Sky pilot' is slang for a chaplain, suiting the religious surface, but here it is literal: a flyer.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally, a pilot of the sky is an aviator, a member of an air force.

clue.text: Short action that may be open and shut?

definitions.text: that may be open and shut

parts.note: brief means short
a case is a legal action in court

explanation.surface: A quick lawsuit might be an open-and-shut case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open and shut' points to an easy legal case, but the definition is literal: a document bag that opens and closes.
explanation.definitionFit: A document bag with a hinged lid is opened and shut as it is used, a whimsical description.

indicators.note: the word goes is placed round the boxer, enclosing him

parts.note: Muhammad Ali, the heavyweight champion boxer

explanation.surface: A boxer goes a round alongside some footballers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' is the container signal, borrowing the boxing sense of a round in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Goalkeepers are footballers, so the plural is a fair example-type definition.

clue.text: Reformed Chapel anthems used to promote the virtues of water

definitions.text: used to promote the virtues of water

indicators.note: the words are re-formed, put together in a different order, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: Revised hymns from a chapel are used to advertise healthy water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reformed' rearranges CHAPELANTHEMS; the religious sense of Reformed is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gloucestershire spa town became famous for promoting its mineral springs and their supposed health benefits.

indicators.note: a reflection shows the word mirror-wise, back to front

parts.note: mode means fashion, as in the latest mode

explanation.surface: An ancient people mirrored the styles of their day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' turns MODE round.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical Edomites, descendants of Esau, were an ancient people of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Fashion from Dior's a help with a round figure

indicators.note: to fashion something from material is to shape it anew, signalling rearrangement

parts.note: Dior's here is Dior is, so the S counts as a letter

explanation.surface: A couturier's help is enlisted to dress a plump customer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion from' rearranges DIORSAHELP; the Dior link to fashion is the decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shaped like a ball or near-ball has a rounded figure.

definitions.meaning: an oily substance that reduces friction
the stage and screen musical of that name, a show for performers to put on

explanation.surface: An oil meant for actors on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Grease is a thick lubricating fat, and the title of a well-known stage musical.

indicators.note: the letters are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Unseasonal rain is falling on the Welsh mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' rearranges RAINFALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Llanfair is a village on Anglesey in North Wales, short for the famously long place name.

clue.text: Foreign cops seem grand, if disorganised

indicators.note: the letters are thrown into disorder, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: Overseas police look impressive, if a bit chaotic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorganised' rearranges SEEMGRAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Gendarmes are French armed police officers, hence foreign cops to a British solver.

parts.note: a disco is a loud dance party

indicators.note: sure is ruined, its letters wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: A loud party certainly makes chat impossible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruins' rearranges SURE to URSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Discourse is spoken exchange, talk between people, a synonym of conversation.

definitions.meaning: a reason or motive for something
Matthew Arnold called Oxford the home of lost ...

explanation.surface: Oxford has long been where reasoning goes astray.
explanation.walkthrough: Matthew Arnold famously called Oxford University the 'home of lost causes'.
explanation.definitionFit: A reason for an event is its origin; and a hopeless campaign is a lost one.

definitions.meaning: Lynne ... wrote the punctuation guide Eats, Shoots and Leaves
to tie up tightly, like poultry or hay, is to bind into a bundle

explanation.surface: A language pedant earns a lot of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes a bundle' suggests making a fortune; it means tying things up.
explanation.definitionFit: Lynne Truss is a writer on punctuation; truss as a verb means tie up tightly.

parts.note: rep is a repertory company of actors, players

indicators.note: a performance of the word over makes something different out of its letters

explanation.surface: A critic condemns the actors for their show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performance' rearranges OVER to ROVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To reprove is to rebuke, a near synonym of the verb censure.

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
uttered means spoken

explanation.surface: Someone talks softly about windows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quiet-spoken' looks like one word for soft-voiced but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Windows fitted with closed panels or blinds are described as shuttered.

indicators.note: fancy as in elaborate or imaginative treatment, rearranging the letters

parts.note: isn't taken as its letters without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A fleeting whim is not true art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges ISNTART; 'Passing fancy' reads as one phrase but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit is the act of passing through or across, as in goods in transit.

parts.note: Erin is a poetic name for Ireland
yes, indeed, an affirmation

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the avenging spirits are found in Ireland, and agrees.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Erinyes are the avenging goddesses the Romans called the Furies.

parts.note: a variation in Elgar's Enigma Variations bears the name of the biblical mighty hunter, a figure hunting lobbyists might revere

explanation.surface: A mysterious supporter of the pro-hunting lobby.
explanation.walkthrough: The Countryside Alliance is a British lobby group supporting fox hunting; Elgar's Enigma Variations includes a famous movement with this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical Nimrod was a mighty hunter, and a movement of Elgar's Enigma Variations shares his name.

clue.text: Is Harpo Marx starting to make a witty sally

indicators.note: the letters are used to make something new, a rearrangement
only the starting letter of Marx is taken

explanation.surface: Harpo Marx, the silent one, is starting to make a quip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' rearranges ISHARPO to APHORIS; 'starting' gives M from Marx. Harpo was the Marx brother who never spoke.
explanation.definitionFit: An aphorism is a pithy saying, and a sally is a witty remark, so the two overlap.

parts.note: an ace is the one in a pack of cards

indicators.note: the help is turned back, rejected, so its word runs backwards

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: A lazy person is the type to turn down assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' turns AID into DIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Acedia is spiritual torpor, the medieval name for the deadly sin of sloth.

indicators.note: the word loner re-forms, its letters taking a new shape

explanation.surface: A solitary person turns over a new leaf and signs up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reforms' rearranges LONER.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrol is to sign up or enlist, a synonym of join up.

clue.text: With nothing sure, grasp fails — but it wasn't worth the effort

indicators.note: the grasp fails, so the letters fall apart and reform

parts.note: O, the zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Without a firm hold, a climber slips and says the summit wasn't worth it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fails' rearranges O with SUREGRASP. The phrase comes from Aesop's fox, who decided the grapes it could not reach were sour anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: Claiming something unattainable was not worth having is the attitude called by this idiom.

indicators.note: the word for uplifting sounds like the answer when spoken

parts.note: an uplifting is a raise, a lifting up

explanation.surface: Sunbeams are said to raise the spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Rays are narrow beams of light, a direct synonym.

definitions.meaning: the captions or key on a map or picture
the ends of the legs are where the feet are

explanation.surface: A caption describing someone's feet.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits as LEG ENDS, the lowest parts of the legs.
explanation.definitionFit: The captions under pictures are called by this word, and the bottoms of the legs are feet.

parts.note: a sty is a pigpen, the hog's home
a list is a register or roll

explanation.surface: A designer draws up a register of pigs.
explanation.definitionFit: A stylist designs hair, clothing or interiors, a type of designer.
